## Suggestion: Acceptance-first charting for user-facing maps

Following up on #25, one more structural gap in the wayfinder macro model that
surfaced in practice: **a map of work is not the same as a map of acceptance.**
For any effort that changes what a user sees or perceives, the board currently
charts *what to build* but never *what counts as accepted* — so a milestone can
reach green while the real, user-visible journey is broken.

This is distinct from #25 (which proposed concrete structural tasks/per-map
conventions). This suggestion is about adding an **acceptance dimension** to the
macro board for user-facing efforts.

## Problem

- The destination clause (ADR-020 "coverage in the destination") is satisfiable
  by buildable leaves that only add scenario coverage against fast/mock adapters.
  Nothing distinguishes a quick mock adapter from a real-route probe, so a
  user-facing milestone can ship with mock-only coverage and unknown real-route
  behavior.
- Buildable `wayfinder:task` leaves describe *what to do*, never *what
  user-visible outcome they evidence, on which real route, and what counts as
  fail vs blocked*. Impl slices can satisfy isolated checks while the integrated
  journey stays broken.
- Acceptance truth is retrofitted after the fact (bolted on as an un-shipped
  prerequisite only after a sloppy delivery), instead of being defined at
  charting time when it is cheapest.

## Proposal

1. **Acceptance contract as a first-class charting artifact.** Every
   user-facing/visual map carries a Shaping-owned acceptance contract drafted at
   charting time (and sharpened at the first HITL/arch-review ticket) — before
   implementation leaves. Even a "simple" visual change requires an independent
   visual-verification acceptance. Internal/surfaceless efforts (refactor,
   config, doc-only) are exempt.
2. **Adapter honesty, encoded as a charting invariant.** Contract rows default
   to real-route. A map may flip specific rows to mock-only only by an explicit
   shaping/grilling decision, and mock rows still carry a mandatory visual
   verdict. Structural truth (a G1-style admission gate) is always real-route.
   Mock evidence can never close a user-visible criterion on its own.
3. **The completion gate is an independent evaluator + human verdict.** The map
   that owns verification should close only when (a) a deterministic evaluator
   runs the acceptance rows against real evidence and returns pass/fail/blocked,
   and (b) a human reviews the produced artifacts (screenshots, evidence) and
   passes. The builder's own self-check (refactor, harness-update) is not the
   gate.
4. **Traceability, best-effort.** Buildable leaves name the criterion IDs they
   evidence where the mapping is known at charting time; fog stays only for what
   cannot be named yet.

## Suggested shape

- Tier A (per-map): the acceptance contract lives on the map/ticket (body +
  linked comment) for fast retrieval — not committed to the tree.
- Tier B (single committed source): ONE committed, versioned "current state of
  the application" design-truth artifact set (the files an admission evaluator
  validates against) that everyone can refer to, rewritten whenever a visual map
  completes. No committed golden screenshots — screenshots are environment-
  brittle and "a screenshot is not the verdict"; stable image baselines only
  after several accepted low-churn runs. Visual reference is provided by linked
  artifacts, not committed reference images.

Worth folding into the wayfinder skill as an acceptance-first constraint for
user-facing maps. Happy to iterate on the exact artifact shape.
title: Suggestion: acceptance-first charting for user-facing maps (contract + evaluator gate + human verdict)

## Suggestion: Enhanced wayfinder charting conventions

This is a suggestion for extending the wayfinder skill's macro-mode charting with structural conventions we've found valuable in practice.

### 1. Two E2E maps per milestone

Every milestone should have at least 2 E2E maps as children:

- **E2E Harness** (automated Playwright): covers the milestone's acceptance criteria with automated tests. Buildable leaves dispatch into SDLC runs. Extends the previous milestone's harness incrementally.
- **E2E Manual** (operator walkthrough): a human drives the app end-to-end as a real user, surfacing UX gaps the harness misses (state desync, HTTP 200 + wrong-body, auth gates, visual issues). Operator-reported issues file as GAP tasks under this map.

E2E maps chain: each milestone's E2E is blocked by the prior milestone's corresponding E2E map. This gates the E2E chain so a milestone's E2E can't start until the previous milestone's E2E has passed.

### 2. Implementation map structure

Each implementation map should include these structural tasks:

1. **Architecture review** (HITL, first task): a grilling ticket where the architect reviews the map's scope against the architecture, ADRs, and existing code. The result may be a sub-map or just tasks. This blocks all other tasks in the map.

2. **Grill-with-docs activation**: when charting tasks, the agent should activate grill-with-docs so that obvious questions (answerable from existing seam artifacts, docs, ADRs, code) don't need a separate grilling ticket. Two field types:
   - **Green field**: no related artifacts exist. Chart research, grilling, and prototype tasks as usual.
   - **Brown field**: similar work done before. High confidence that correct context can be injected. Surface all tasks — grill-with-docs resolves obvious questions without HITL overhead.

3. **Refactoring task** (near-last task): checks deliverables against the map's acceptance criteria. Ensures code follows ADRs, no code smell left behind. Buildable leaf that blocks on all other tasks being done.

4. **E2E harness update task** (last task): updates the E2E harness so that when the milestone nears completion, the harness already contains all acceptance criteria. Note: E2E manual may surface more missing E2E, so the E2E harness map could have a sub-map inside.

### 3. Board healing protocol

When asked to heal the board:
1. Render the tree and identify stranded nodes (detached, no parent)
2. Wire stranded nodes to their correct parent via sub-issue API
3. Close finished-but-open maps that block siblings
4. Verify no orphan issues (open wayfinder tickets with no parent, not root)
5. If unsure which node should come next, ask for priority

### Why these conventions

In practice, we found that:
- Automated harness alone misses operator-facing issues (state desync, visual gaps). A manual walkthrough map catches what the harness can't.
- Maps without an architecture review upfront tend to discover scope problems mid-implementation, wasting SDLC runs.
- Maps without a refactoring task accumulate code smell and ADR violations.
- Maps without an E2E harness update task arrive at milestone completion with no acceptance coverage, forcing a rushed harness authoring phase.
- Grill-with-docs activation distinguishes "we've done this before" (brown field, surface all tasks) from "this is new" (green field, research/prototype first), reducing unnecessary HITL overhead.

These conventions are opt-in per project (declared in the map's Notes, like `mode: macro`) and do not change the base wayfinder skill's behavior for projects that don't adopt them.

## Summary

This gap analysis covers **model provisioning for the SDLC agent dispatchers** in Loom — specifically two related concerns that a real deployment surfaced and that upstream has no first-class mechanism for yet:

1. **Provider rotation with quota/window awareness** — dispatching agent work onto the right model *given which provider still has headroom*, when every provider is a flat-rate subscription with a reset window rather than metered pay-as-you-go.
2. **Per-agent reasoning-effort tuning** — setting extended-thinking depth per agent role, and reconciling it with a model router that can move an agent across providers.

Both are mechanical, deployment-agnostic, and currently solved with bespoke glue in the deployment rather than anything upstream provides. This issue proposes them as first-class Loom concepts.

---

## Background: the deployment reality this addresses

A Loom deployment runs its SDLC dispatchers (planner, orchestrator, executors, verifier) against several LLM providers. Two facts drive the gap:

- **Providers are flat-rate subscriptions with reset windows**, not metered per-token billing. E.g. provider A resets ~every 5 hours, provider B every 7 days. "Cost" is therefore *how much of each window's quota is used*, and the failure mode is bricking a run when the primary's window just reset or exhausted.
- **Model capability is tiered.** A "frontier" model is overkill for trivial mechanical edits; a "budget" model is insufficient for high-judgment verification. Every agent role has a natural reasoning-depth.

A naive config fixes each agent to one model. That leaves quota idle on some buckets while others exhaust, and forces manual intervention when a window resets mid-run.

---

## Gap 1: No first-class "model rotation with quota awareness"

**What upstream has:** Each agent declares a single static `model:` (a `provider/model` string). The agent runs on exactly that model.

**What the deployment needed:** An ordered, per-agent fallback list, evaluated at dispatch time against *which provider still has headroom this window*. Concretely:

- A per-agent **ordered preference array** of `provider/model` candidates (e.g. for a mechanical executor: budget-first, then frontier only as a last resort).
- A **quota/window probe** per candidate: is the provider authenticated, is it past its window cap (a rolling per-window usage ledger), and has it recently errored with quota/rate-limit/token-limit?
- **Pin the first ready candidate** into the agent's `model:` line (which, because agent definitions are tracked files, must be applied across the main checkout *and* every worktree/active branch).

**Why upstream should own it:** The probe logic, the "pin across worktrees" mechanic, and the fail-closed behavior (if *every* candidate is exhausted, do not dispatch — surface instead of silently running on a degraded model) are all deployment-agnostic. Currently each deployment hand-rolls a rotation script; that glue should be a Loom utility or documented pattern.

**Design sketch:**

- Agent frontmatter gains an optional ordered `models:` list (fallback candidates), while `model:` stays the "pinned / currently-active" value.
- A dispatch helper resolves `models:` → the first candidate whose provider has window headroom, and pins it.
- A small usage ledger records per-window token consumption per provider so the probe is not just "did the last call fail?".

---

## Gap 2: Per-agent reasoning-effort is undocumented and provider-dependent

**What upstream has:** The agent spec (and the OpenCode config schema) supports a per-agent `reasoningEffort` pass-through field, and models expose named variants. But Loom's generated agent files carry no guidance on how to set reasoning depth per role, and the interaction with model rotation is unaddressed.

**What the deployment needed:**

- A **role→reasoning-effort mapping** as a documented default, e.g.:
  - *Verifier / reviewer* → highest (deep codebase + impact + latent-bug scrutiny).
  - *Orchestrator / dispatcher* → high (unexpected events, quality gates).
  - *Hard-problem executor* → high.
  - *Planner / designer* → medium (judgment, low blast radius).
  - *Mechanical executor / recon* → default/medium (extra thinking is pure overhead on bounded tasks).
- A clear **mechanism**, since two competing syntaxes exist in the wild: a `provider/model#variant` suffix and a `reasoningEffort:` field. Only the field is reliably honored; the suffix is not portable across providers and can error.

**Why upstream should own it:** The *default mapping* is generic agent-design guidance (which role deserves deep thinking). The *mechanism* needs documenting so deployments don't guess. And critically:

**Gap 2b — rotation × reasoning interaction.** When a model router moves an agent from a frontier provider to a budget provider mid-window, the reasoning-effort setting must not leak a value the fallback provider doesn't understand. The clean design: reasoning effort lives as a **field independent of the model** (so it survives rotation), and the router is responsible for *dropping or remapping* it when the pinned model's provider doesn't support the requested tier. This interaction is currently unhandled and un-documented.

---

## Gap 3 (smaller): "select the right agent for the job" is left entirely to the dispatcher prompt

The SDLC workflow already describes dispatcher agents that route work to executor subagents by difficulty. But the concrete **selection table** (which agent class handles which task size / risk profile) is prose in a prompt, not a checkable artifact. A deployment that wants determinism ("trivial single-file → fast executor; architectural → deep executor; needs pixel proof → vision QA") has to reinvent and hand-maintain that table.

**Proposal:** a documented, reusable *agent-selection rubric* (task-size × risk → agent class) that dispatcher prompts reference, so the routing decision is mechanical and auditable rather than vibes.

---

## Suggested scope for upstream to consider

- Document the per-agent `reasoningEffort` mechanism and a **default role→effort mapping** (Gap 2).
- Add an optional ordered `models:` fallback list to the agent spec, plus a **quota-aware model-resolution helper** and a per-window usage ledger (Gap 1).
- Specify the **rotation × reasoning interaction**: how the router preserves/remaps reasoning effort across provider moves (Gap 2b).
- Add a reusable **agent-selection rubric** referenced by dispatcher prompts (Gap 3).

These are generic agent-operations concerns — applicable to any multi-agent SDLC deployment that runs against multiple flat-rate LLM providers, regardless of the specific models or product in question.
title: Gap analysis: quota-aware model rotation and per-agent reasoning-effort tuning for SDLC dispatchers

## Summary

This issue captures the gaps discovered between a real-world Loom deployment and the upstream framework, based on a full audit of the upstream `adapters/hermes/`, `adapters/opencode/`, `contract/`, `workflows/`, `wiki/adr/`, and `SKILLS/` against the local `.opencode/`, `.loom/`, `AGENTS.md`, and the resident PM Agent deployment on a Hermes server.

The deployment uses a **three-actor topology**:
1. **On-demand assistant** (Hermes agent, CLI-invoked, not cron-driven)
2. **PM Agent** (separate Hermes agent in a container — resident macro-PM tick loop, hourly cron)
3. **SDLC** (OpenCode CLI — per-invocation, headless-dispatchable micro target)

---

## Gap Analysis

### GAP 1: `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` does not exist on disk

**What upstream says:** The Hermes adapter (setup.md Output) and OpenCode adapter (MAPPING.md §7) both mandate that `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` is **always generated** — it names the source of truth, the micro dispatch target, the label scheme, and the ledger root. The OpenCode adapter also lists it in `opencode.json`'s `instructions:` array.

**What we have:** `AGENTS.md` has two loom provenance sections that both reference `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md`, but `.loom/` is gitignored and the directory **does not exist on disk**. No `protocol.md`, no `index.md` manifest. The `opencode.json` `instructions:` array does not point at it.

**Impact:** The seam-artifact protocol has no concrete instance. Any SDLC run that tries to DISCOVER a shaping artifact at its entry gate finds nothing. Any PM Agent tick that tries to PRODUCE a `shaping/<milestone>/` seam artifact has no ledger to write to.

**Suggested fix:** Run a loom `update` (both adapters) to regenerate the protocol document and manifest on disk. Since `.loom/` is gitignored, this is a local-only initialization step.

---

### GAP 2: Hermes adapter was never formally run — no `wayfinder-macro` profile distribution

**What upstream says:** The Hermes adapter renders a `wayfinder-macro` resident profile (`config.yaml` + `SOUL.md` + macro-PM skills) delivered as a **profile distribution** (git repo installed via `hermes profile install`). The `SOUL.md` carries the tick-loop prose, the one-source-of-truth directive, the capability note, and the altitude-seam handoff note. The `config.yaml` carries `model.default` + `model.fallback_providers:` + the prescribed toolsets with **`write_file`/`patch` disabled** (the load-bearing no-code-edit withhold).

**What we have:** The PM Agent runs in a Docker container with an hourly cron tick loop. It was set up **manually** — not through the loom Hermes adapter's guided setup. The `AGENTS.md` has a `<!-- loom:setup-hermes:begin -->` section that was hand-written, not adapter-generated. There is no profile distribution repo, no `SOUL.md` from the template, no `config.yaml` with the prescribed toolset composition + per-tool withhold.

**Impact:**
- The PM Agent's configuration may not enforce the load-bearing no-code-edit withhold. If the PM Agent can `write_file`/`patch`, the forcing function that keeps it routing rather than building is absent.
- The one-source-of-truth directive and altitude-seam handoff instructions are not formally encoded in a `SOUL.md`.
- No fallback model provider chain — a model deprecation breaks the tick loop.

**Suggested fix:** Run the Hermes adapter's `init`/`update` against the PM Agent to formally generate the `wayfinder-macro` profile, or at minimum validate the existing manual setup against the adapter's verify checklist (`adapters/hermes/references/verify.md`).

---

### GAP 3: Label vocabularies may not be fully provisioned on the tracker

**What upstream says:** The Hermes adapter (macro-pm.md §4f) requires provisioning two label vocabularies on the tracker:
- **Down:** `wayfinder:research`, `wayfinder:prototype`, `wayfinder:grilling`, `wayfinder:task`, `wayfinder:map`
- **Up:** `sdlc:in-progress`, `sdlc:done`, `sdlc:needs-recharter`, `sdlc:needs-clarification`
- **Third origin:** `qa:regression-failed`

**What we have:** The project board uses `wayfinder:*` labels but also runs a custom scheme — board Status columns (Backlog→Refinement→Ready→In Progress→In Review→Done) and priority labels (P0/P1/P2) with role tags. The upstream `sdlc:*` return vocabulary may not be provisioned.

**Impact:** The PM Agent's tick loop cannot mechanically route `sdlc:*` returns from SDLC runs if those labels don't exist. The two-vocabulary seam depends on both vocabularies being present.

**Suggested fix:** Verify which labels exist on the tracker and provision missing ones. If the project runs a different scheme, map onto it and record the mapping in the protocol document's macro section.

---

### GAP 4: No `opencode.json` `instructions:` pointer to the protocol document

**What upstream says:** The OpenCode adapter (MAPPING.md §7, STAGES.md protocol section) requires `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` in `opencode.json`'s `instructions:` array so it merges into always-on context for every SDLC agent.

**What we have:** The `opencode.json` does not include `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` in its `instructions:` array.

**Impact:** SDLC stage agents (Shaping, Planner, Orchestrator, Closing) would not know where the ledger lives, what the namespace convention is, or what artifacts each stage should produce/discover at the seams.

**Suggested fix:** Add `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` to the `instructions:` array in `opencode.json` (after generating the protocol document per GAP 1).

---

### GAP 5: No reachable artifact ref substrate (`loom-artifacts/<map-slug>`)

**What upstream says:** ADR-022 mandates that HITL ticket outputs publish to a **reachable networked artifact ref** — an orphan branch `loom-artifacts/<map-slug>` on the git host — and the ticket links the URL. A link to a local-only path (`.loom/…`) is a **protocol violation**.

**What we have:** `AGENTS.md` mentions orphan branch refs `loom-artifacts/<map-slug>`, so the concept is known. However, there is no evidence that HITL ticket outputs have been published to such refs. The `.loom/` directory doesn't exist either.

**Impact:** If the PM Agent resolves a grilling/prototype ticket and writes output to a local path (or nowhere), the dispatched SDLC run cannot reach it across the harness boundary. The baton drops at the altitude seam — the exact failure ADR-022 prevents.

**Suggested fix:** Implement the artifact-ref publishing workflow: when the PM Agent resolves a HITL ticket, PRODUCE the artifact to `loom-artifacts/<map-slug>` orphan branch and link the URL from the ticket.

---

### GAP 6: The on-demand assistant has no formal role in the Loom topology

**What upstream says:** The Hermes adapter renders exactly one profile — the `wayfinder-macro` resident agent. The on-demand assistant is a separate Hermes agent that is NOT the PM Agent and NOT an SDLC agent. It doesn't fit any of the three archetypes (resident macro, per-invocation SDLC, or utility subagent).

**What we have:** The on-demand assistant is a Hermes agent invoked from CLI. It manages the PM Agent remotely and assists with the project. It has no loom-generated profile, no `SOUL.md` from the adapter, and no formal role in the SDLC or macro-PM topology. It exists in a gap the framework doesn't name.

**Impact:** This is an **unnamed actor** in the Loom topology. The framework has:
- Resident agents (PM Agent — macro altitude)
- Per-invocation SDLC agents (OpenCode — micro altitude)
- Utility subagents (explore/quick/deep/verifier — dispatched within SDLC)

But there is no named role for a **human-facing operations assistant** that manages the resident agent and the project from a different altitude than either macro or micro. The on-demand assistant is effectively a **third altitude** — an "ops" altitude that sits beside the macro/micro split, managing infrastructure and board state, but Loom has no concept for it.

**Suggested fix (framework-level):** Options:
1. **Name it:** Add a named role (e.g. "ops assistant") to the harness-archetypes taxonomy for an on-demand agent that manages resident agents and project infrastructure without being part of the SDLC or macro-PM loop.
2. **Fold it:** Document that the on-demand assistant is a Hermes profile outside Loom's lifecycle scope by design — but then the framework should say so explicitly.
3. **Adapt:** Consider whether the on-demand assistant should be a second resident profile — but that raises whether Loom's "thin-macro" adapter should render more than one profile.

---

### GAP 7: No drift detection or `update` reconciliation process

**What upstream says:** The Hermes adapter (setup.md) and contract (index.md) define an `update` mode that detects drift — what changed in Loom **and** in the project — and patches in place. The provenance markers (`<!-- loom:setup-opencode:begin -->` / `<!-- loom:setup-hermes:begin -->`) are the mechanism for idempotent patching.

**What we have:** The provenance markers exist in `AGENTS.md`, but there's no record of a formal `update` run. The `.opencode/agents/*.md` files were last modified Aug 23 with no git commits touching `.opencode/` since. The upstream CHANGELOG shows several changes since then (ADR-022, ADR-023, ADR-024) that should have triggered an `update` but apparently didn't.

**Impact:** The local `.opencode/` tree is stale. Specifically:
- ADR-023 added `shell` (`bash: allow`) to `explore` — our `explore.md` has `bash: deny` (pre-ADR-023)
- ADR-024 added spec-fidelity verification to the Verifier — our `verifier.md` may not reference it

**Suggested fix:** Run a Loom `update` (both adapters) against the current upstream to reconcile drift.

---

### GAP 8: OpenCode `explore` agent has `bash: deny` — contradicts ADR-023

**What upstream says:** ADR-023 added `shell` to the `explore` utility's capability set: `read`, `search`, `shell` — no `edit`, no `delegate`. The `bash: allow` grant lets dispatched recon run `gh issue view`, `git log/diff/blame`, and project read commands. The read-only guarantee is the **withheld `edit`**, not the absence of shell.

**What we have:** `.opencode/agents/explore.md` has `bash: deny` — the pre-ADR-023 configuration.

**Impact:** Recon dispatched to `@explore` cannot run `gh`, `git`, or project read commands. The work bounces back to the expensive Shaping agent, defeating the read-only research orchestrator pattern (ADR-021).

**Suggested fix:** Change `explore.md` from `bash: deny` to `bash: allow` (keeping `edit: deny`).

---

## Summary table

| # | Gap | Severity | Actor affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` missing on disk | Critical | All — seam protocol has no instance |
| 2 | PM Agent profile not adapter-generated | High | PM Agent — no formal SOUL.md/config/withhold |
| 3 | Label vocabularies may be incomplete | High | PM Agent — mechanical routing breaks |
| 4 | No `opencode.json` `instructions:` pointer | High | SDLC agents — protocol document invisible |
| 5 | No artifact-ref publishing implemented | High | PM Agent + SDLC — baton drops at altitude seam |
| 6 | On-demand assistant has no named Loom role | Medium | Framework — unnamed third altitude |
| 7 | No drift detection / update reconciliation | Medium | All — stale config vs upstream |
| 8 | `explore` agent has `bash: deny` (pre-ADR-023) | Medium | SDLC — recon can't run shell commands |

---

## Context

This gap analysis was produced by auditing the upstream Loom framework against a real-world three-actor deployment (on-demand assistant + PM Agent + SDLC). The topology is a deployment of Loom's resident + per-invocation harness archetypes, and the gaps above are the delta between the framework's design and the deployment's current state.

Gaps 1-5 and 7-8 are deployment-level issues that can be resolved by running the adapters' `update` mode and provisioning the missing substrate. Gap 6 is a **framework-level** observation: Loom's harness-archetypes taxonomy names resident and per-invocation harnesses, but does not name the "on-demand ops assistant" archetype that this deployment uses. This is raised as a `wayfinder:grilling` ticket because Gap 6 requires a design decision (name it, fold it, or adapt the taxonomy), and the other gaps are actionable findings that fall out of the same audit.

Blocked by: #20

## Question

Update the macro-PM tick seed to call the shipped `loom board` verbs instead of the raw-`gh` "rung-1 bootstrap" prose:

- `workflows/macro-pm/index.md` — the tick loop section.
- `SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md` macro mode — "Board mutation" language.
- `.mirai/agents/wayfinder-macro.agent.md` — replace the inline `gh label create …` bootstrap and raw `gh issue …` reasoning with calls to `loom board` verbs at each named tick step (Reconcile → Read → Route → Act → Integrate → Reconcile → Exit).
- `adapters/hermes/` references that describe the resident tick loop.

Keep the seed **prose + illustrative pseudo-code only** — never embed `scripts/loom/`'s executable contents into the seed (ADR-025 decision #5). Run `bash scripts/validate.sh` after edits.

This is a **buildable leaf**, dispatched into an SDLC run once the build leaf (this map's other `task` ticket) has closed.

---

**Contract update (2026-09-09)** — the CLI contract is now decided ([resolution](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/19#issuecomment-5596109488), [ADR-025](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/blob/main/wiki/adr/adr-025-deterministic-board-api.md) Accepted). Wire the seed to these exact spellings:

```
node scripts/loom/index.js board read [--frontier]
node scripts/loom/index.js board tree [--format=tree|mermaid]
node scripts/loom/index.js board apply <ticket> <transition>
node scripts/loom/index.js board reconcile [--dry-run]
```

- The tool lives at **`scripts/loom/`** and the verbs are **namespaced** (`loom board …`) per [ADR-027](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/blob/main/wiki/adr/adr-027-mechanism-install-port.md) — never a standalone `board` binary.
- **Four verbs, not five**: `heal` is gone; `reconcile` is the single name.
- The tick shape is now **bookended**: `Reconcile → Read → Route → Act → Integrate → Reconcile → Exit` — the same call at both ends. Update every place the old `Heal → … → Reconcile` shape is written, including the glossary's *Manual tick* and *Board heal / reconcile* entries.
- `apply`'s six transitions are `claim`, `dispatch`, `close --pointer <url>`, `graduate-recharter`, `open-clarification`, `seed-regression-map` — the seed's dispatch prose should name these, never raw labels.

## Question

Build **`scripts/loom/`** — a Node.js distributable implementing the four ADR-025 board verbs against plain GitHub Issues via `gh`:

```
node scripts/loom/index.js board read [--frontier]
node scripts/loom/index.js board tree [--format=tree|mermaid]
node scripts/loom/index.js board apply <ticket> <transition>
node scripts/loom/index.js board reconcile [--dry-run]
```

**The full CLI contract is decided — build to it exactly:** see the [resolution comment on the contract ticket](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/19#issuecomment-5596109488) and [ADR-025](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/blob/main/wiki/adr/adr-025-deterministic-board-api.md) (now **Accepted**). It fixes the six transition names, the normalised JSON envelope and ticket shape, the tiered exit codes, and `apply`'s idempotency preconditions. Do not re-derive any of it.

### Load-bearing points a builder must not get wrong

- **`scripts/loom/`, namespaced — not `scripts/board/`, not a standalone `board`.** [ADR-027](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/blob/main/wiki/adr/adr-027-mechanism-install-port.md) (Accepted) mandates a *single* Mechanism-layer distributable exposing namespaced verbs; `REGISTRY.md` already registers `loom size score`, which graduates into this same tree later. `board` is a namespace, not a binary.
- **No packaging.** No `package.json`, no `bin` entry, no npm, no install step, no dependencies beyond what `gh` itself needs. Invoked by path.
- **Four verbs, not five.** `heal` was dropped; `reconcile` is the single name for the detect-drift → repair operation.
- **`apply` hides all label knowledge.** Callers name intent (`claim`, `dispatch`, `close --pointer <url>`, `graduate-recharter`, `open-clarification`, `seed-regression-map`); the tool owns every `wayfinder:*` / `sdlc:*` string. No raw `labels` in output either.
- **Keyless** — relies on `gh auth`, inherits `gh`'s cwd-derived repo context, `--repo owner/name` as optional override. No separate API key ([ADR-010](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/blob/main/wiki/adr/adr-010-keyless-by-default-recommendations.md)).
- **Use `gh`'s native flags, not GraphQL.** As of `gh` 2.98.0, `gh issue create --parent` and `gh issue edit --parent/--add-blocked-by/--add-blocking` are native. The earlier "must use the `addSubIssue` GraphQL mutation" finding is **stale** — do not build a GraphQL path. BFS over `subIssues` still applies for *reading* full trees.
- Every verb emits JSON except `tree`'s human-facing render, and exits nonzero on drift/conflict.

This is a **buildable leaf** in macro mode — dispatch it into an SDLC run rather than building it in the map session (the charting/tick agent has no `edit` capability).

## Question

What is the exact `gh` CLI + GraphQL surface this distributable should wrap for each of the five verbs, and what does each need to emit as JSON?

Specifically:
- **`board read [--frontier]`**: `gh issue list --label wayfinder:map` for roots; per-root, GraphQL `issue.subIssues` for children (confirmed working: `repository(...) { issue(number:N) { subIssues { nodes { number title } } } }`); a child's `wayfinder:<type>` label gives its kind; unblocked = every issue named in a `Blocked by: #n` body line is closed. What's the minimal GraphQL query (or `gh api`) to fetch labels + assignees + body + closed-state for a root's whole subtree in as few round-trips as possible?
- **`board tree`**: same data as `read`, rendered two ways — an indented Unicode tree, and a Mermaid `graph TD` block. What's a clean recursive-render algorithm given the subIssues nesting?
- **`board apply <ticket> <transition>`**: enumerate the concrete `gh issue edit`/`gh issue comment`/`gh issue close` calls needed for each transition the dispatch table names (claim = `--add-assignee @me`; set `sdlc:in-progress`; close + comment on `sdlc:done`; etc.) — what's the full transition vocabulary implied by [wayfinder macro mode](../../SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md#the-two-vocabulary-seam) and this agent's routing table?
- **`board heal`/`board reconcile`**: what drift signatures are detectable purely from `gh`/GraphQL reads (e.g. `sdlc:in-progress` leaf + a resolution comment already present; an issue with both an open-state label and a closed state) and what's the idempotent repair for each?

Findings should include concrete command/query snippets ready to lift into implementation, and confirm `gh auth status` is sufficient (no separate API key — keyless per [ADR-010](../../wiki/adr/adr-010-keyless-by-default-recommendations.md)).

body:
## Destination

The [ADR-025](../../wiki/adr/adr-025-deterministic-board-api.md) **board-API distributable** — verbs `read [--frontier]` / `tree` / `apply <ticket> <transition>` / `reconcile`, a thin Node.js wrapper over `gh` for plain GitHub Issues (sub-issues + `Blocked by: #n` lines, no Projects v2 board) — is built at `scripts/loom/` (the `board` verb namespace). The macro-PM tick seed (`workflows/macro-pm/index.md`, `SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md` macro mode, `.mirai/agents/wayfinder-macro.agent.md`, and the Hermes adapter's tick-loop references) is updated to call the shipped verbs instead of reasoning through raw `gh` invocations — replacing the "rung-1 bootstrap" language. And its CLI user journeys are guarded by passing checks in the standing regression suite (coverage clause — a CLI is a user-perceivable surface).

## Notes

- Domain: [ADR-025](../../wiki/adr/adr-025-deterministic-board-api.md) (the decision), [workflows/macro-pm/index.md](../../workflows/macro-pm/index.md) (the tick loop this replaces raw-gh reasoning in), [SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md](../../SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md#macro-mode-dispatching-into-sdlc-runs) (the dispatch table `board apply` executes), [wiki/glossary/index.md](../../wiki/glossary/index.md#board-api) (Board API / Manual tick / Board heal-reconcile entries).
- `mode: macro` — this map's `task` tickets are buildable leaves dispatched into SDLC runs (the charting agent has no `edit` capability; building happens one altitude down).
- Locked from interview: **Node.js**, living at `scripts/loom/` as the `board` verb namespace (not `scripts/board/`, not a top-level `board-api/`) — see the CLI-contract resolution, thin wrapper over `gh` (no new external deps beyond what `gh` itself needs). All verbs ship as **one** buildable leaf, not split (now **four**, after `heal`/`reconcile` collapsed). Prose wiring of the tick seed to the shipped tool is **in scope** for this map (destination isn't reached until the seed prose points at the real tool).
- Skills every session should consult: [research](../../SKILLS/discovery/research/SKILL.md) (the gh/GraphQL inventory ticket), [grill-with-docs](../../SKILLS/discovery/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) (the CLI-contract design ticket), [design-an-interface](../../SKILLS/design/design-an-interface/SKILL.md) (shaping the verb contract), [derive-e2e-coverage](../../SKILLS/verification/derive-e2e-coverage/SKILL.md) (the e2e-authoring leaf), [contract/PORTS.md](../../contract/PORTS.md) port 1 (`capability→tool` — how an adapter installs/points at this distributable).
- Keyless by default ([ADR-010](../../wiki/adr/adr-010-keyless-by-default-recommendations.md)): auth via `gh auth`, no separate API key.
- Prose-first constraint: the tick seed holds only the CLI **contract** (illustrative pseudo-code); executable code lives in `scripts/board/`, never embedded in the seed (ADR-025 decision #5).

## Decisions so far

- [Research: gh CLI + GraphQL surface for the five board verbs](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/18) — `subIssues` is one-level only (BFS required for full trees); concrete `gh`/GraphQL command per transition confirmed live against this repo; keyless (`gh auth`) confirmed sufficient throughout. **Superseded 2026-09-04 (`gh` 2.98.0):** the original "no `gh issue create --parent` flag, must use the `addSubIssue` GraphQL mutation" finding is **stale** — `gh issue create --parent` and `gh issue edit --parent/--add-blocked-by/--add-blocking` are all native now, so **no GraphQL path is needed** for creation, parenting, or blocking edges (see the correction comment on [the CLI-contract ticket](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/19#issuecomment-5540589915)). BFS-over-`subIssues` still stands for *reading* full trees.
- [Design the `scripts/board/` CLI contract (verbs, transitions, JSON shape, exit codes)](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/19) — the CLI contract is **decided** ([full contract](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/19#issuecomment-5596109488)): entrypoint `node scripts/loom/index.js board <verb>`, **namespaced under `loom`** per [ADR-027](../../wiki/adr/adr-027-mechanism-install-port.md) and living at **`scripts/loom/`** (not `scripts/board/`), with **no packaging** (no `package.json`/`bin`/npm); **four** verbs not five (`heal` dropped, `reconcile` is the single name) so the tick shape is now bookended `Reconcile → … → Reconcile`; six intent-named transitions hiding all label knowledge; normalised loom-native JSON with a `takeable` predicate and no raw `labels`; tiered exit codes (`0`/`1`/`2` conflict-drift/`3` precondition). [ADR-025](../../wiki/adr/adr-025-deterministic-board-api.md) amended accordingly and moved **Proposed → Accepted**.

## Not yet specified

- How each adapter (Mirai, Hermes, OpenCode) actually installs/points at the distributable once built — a port-1-shaped obligation (`capability→tool` discovery discipline) not yet drawn.
- A version-pinning policy for the distributable (how a consumer pins/checks its version) — deferred: `--version` exists but no scheme is set, and no second consumer exists yet.
- A second-tracker backend abstraction (Linear/Notion) behind the same verb contract — deferred per ADR-025's YAGNI stance; revisit only if a second tracker actually arrives.

## Out of scope

- Linear/Notion or any tracker backend beyond plain GitHub Issues (ADR-025: additional backends land only when a second tracker actually arrives).
- Driving a GitHub Projects v2 board (single-select status fields, project item IDs) instead of plain Issues — ADR-025 rejected this alternative; the graph is native sub-issues + `Blocked by:` lines only.
- An MCP server as the mutation core — ADR-025 keeps MCP as an optional *later* consumption layer, never the determinism core (MCP tools are freeform-intent, the opposite of what this ships).
- A hook-based enforcement mechanism forcing calls around the tool — ADR-025 rejected this; Hermes has no hook primitive (only cron/gateway), so the tick prose itself is the only available schedule.
- Auto-posting `board tree`'s Mermaid output back to the map issue — resolved in the CLI contract: `tree` is read-only with zero side effects (it would otherwise fight `reconcile` for map-body ownership). If wanted later it earns its own verb (`loom board publish-tree`).

## Problem

A remote GitHub issue triage run can execute under the loom Shaping primary agent. After the triage decisions and tracker updates are complete, the generic Shaping exit obligation can still produce `.loom/handoffs/shaping/<slug>/` plus a local manifest row.

That local artifact is redundant with the remote issue comments/status and is not reachable by participants outside the current filesystem. For tracker-only triage, it creates a second context source and contradicts the reachability invariant.

## Reproduction

1. Run `/triage` for a GitHub issue under the Shaping agent.
2. Resolve all maintainer questions.
3. Post decision comments and update labels/project state remotely.
4. Complete the run.
5. Observe a local Shaping seam artifact being produced even though no Delivery baton exists.

## Desired behavior

- Remote triage decisions, briefs, labels, and statuses remain canonical on the configured issue tracker.
- A status/decision-only triage run does **not** invoke `stage-handoff` or write a local ledger artifact.
- `stage-handoff` remains mandatory only when triage actually hands implementation work across the Shaping to Delivery seam.
- Normal triage context uses tracker comments. Bulky outputs such as prototypes may use the existing reachable orphan-ref substrate and link from the issue.
- If tracker update fails, triage reports the failure rather than silently falling back to local context passing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The triage skill explicitly distinguishes tracker completion from a Shaping to Delivery handoff.
- [ ] A remote decision-only triage eval produces no `.loom/handoffs/**` artifact.
- [ ] Every resolved question is recoverable from the issue thread and tracker state.
- [ ] An actual ready-for-delivery triage path still produces the formal seam artifact expected by the Planner.
- [ ] Guidance preserves the existing comment-first / orphan-ref-for-bulky-content split.

## Out of scope

- Replacing loom substrate architecture globally.
- Changing checkpoint or within-stage dispatch behavior.
- Mandating one network storage shape for prototypes and other multi-file artifacts.

body:
## Failure mode

When a PR claims "closes #X", the verifier checks correctness (does the code work, is it well-written, security gaps) but does **not** check spec fidelity — does the PR match #X's acceptance criteria. Spec-vs-implementation deltas slip past and surface only as manual follow-ups.

## Evidence

On `zentetsukenz/affiliate-project`, issue #34 spec required token validation regex `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. PR #59 shipped `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` — **two** deviations from spec:

1. **Missing `{1,64}` length cap.** Caught as a manual follow-up (#60 → PR #66).
2. **Uppercase class `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` vs spec `[a-z0-9_-]`.** Lingered until PR #69 — never explicitly reconciled in writing until then.

The verifier passed PR #59. Both deltas were spec-vs-implementation gaps the verifier should have surfaced. The length-cap gap was caught by a human review after the fact; the uppercase gap was pragmatically correct for UUID `tenant_id`s but was still an un-reconciled spec deviation that sat unresolved for a week.

## Proposed enhancement

Add a **spec-fidelity pass** to the verification procedure. When the artifact under review closes an issue:

1. Fetch the closing issue (`gh issue view <N> --json body` or equivalent).
2. Extract its acceptance criteria.
3. For each criterion, report: **matches / deviates / not-addressed**.

**Deviations are flagged evidence for the dispatcher to route on — NOT automatic failures.** The uppercase-class case above is the reason: `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` was pragmatically correct for UUIDs even though it deviated from the literal spec. Surface-the-delta lets the orchestrator/human decide whether the deviation is intentional; auto-failing would reject pragmatically-correct code for literalism. This matches the existing pattern (verifier reports structured evidence, orchestrator decides) and the `edit: deny` constraint.

## Placement

Either:

- **`verification-before-completion` skill, phase 4** ("Success criteria (adversarial)") — currently generic ("re-read the plan/criteria, check each line-by-line"). Issue-tracker awareness (`gh issue view`) may be too environment-specific for the shared skill.
- **Verifier agent prompt** — the tracker-aware layer on top of the shared skill.

Upstream to decide. The concern is that the skill stays generic while the tracker-aware bit lives where `gh` is a native tongue.

## Scope

This is one pass, not a rewrite. The verifier already returns structured evidence; spec-fidelity is one more evidence category in that report.

## Problem

The `@explore` subagent (loom's thin read-only recon utility, `.opencode/agents/explore.md`) is documented as a recon + Q&A utility, but its actual toolset in OpenCode excludes any terminal/shell capability. Its available tools are limited to:

```
{glob, grep, read, list_mcp_resource_templates, list_mcp_resources, read_mcp_resource}
```

There is **no Bash/terminal tool**. This means `@explore` cannot run:
- `gh issue view` / `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` / `gh run view` — GitHub CLI operations
- `git log` / `git diff` / `git blame` — git history queries
- `mix test` / `mix credo` / `mix sobelow` — project quality commands
- Any shell command at all

## Evidence

Observed twice in a single session (2026-08-17) during a wayfinder grilling session on `affiliate-project` issue #70:

1. **First dispatch** — asked `@explore` to read path_safety code AND run `git log --oneline -15 fix/issue-70-symlinked-ancestors`. The agent read the files fine but reported: *"The explore utility in this harness has no Bash tool — I cannot run shell commands. [...] To run `git log`, route the request back through the dispatcher."*

2. **Second dispatch** — asked `@explore` to fetch issue #34, #63, and PR #97 via `gh` CLI. The agent reported: *"I can't return the requested output verbatim because this session exposes no shell or terminal tool, so I cannot execute the `gh` commands."*

Both dispatches had to fall back to the parent (Shaping) agent running the commands directly, defeating the purpose of delegating recon to a cheaper utility tier.

## Impact

- **Broken delegation contract:** The Shaping/Planning agents delegate recon legwork to `@explore` to keep their own context lean. When `@explore` can't run shell commands, the work bounces back to the parent — wasting the parent's context budget on raw output the utility was supposed to absorb.
- **`gh` CLI is the project's tracker access mechanism** (per `.loom/handoffs/protocol.md` macro section). An `@explore` agent that can't run `gh` can't read issues, PRs, or CI runs — the most common recon task during wayfinder/grilling sessions.
- **Git history queries** (`git log`, `git blame`, `git diff`) are standard recon. `@explore` can't do them.

## Expected behavior

`@explore` should have read-only terminal access (a Bash tool with no write/mutation capability) so it can run:
- `gh` commands (issue/PR/CI reads)
- `git` read commands (`log`, `diff`, `blame`, `show`)
- Project read commands (`mix test --failed`, `mix credo`, `cat`, `ls`)

The agent definition in `.opencode/agents/explore.md` should either:
- **(a)** Include a read-only Bash tool in its toolset (preferred — matches the "thin recon" intent), or
- **(b)** Document the limitation explicitly so dispatchers know to route shell-command recon to `@quick` or `@deep` instead of `@explore`.

## Environment

- loom setup: OpenCode harness
- Agent: `@explore` (`.opencode/agents/explore.md`, `mode: subagent`, Utility tier)
- Observed in: `affiliate-project` session, 2026-08-17
- OpenCode CLI v1.18.14

body:
## Destination

A **second loom adapter** — `adapters/opencode/` — that renders loom's SDLC content into OpenCode-native config (`.opencode/`, `opencode.json`) **plus** an opt-in `oh-my-openagent.json` (OMO's "models-are-developers" tiering + agent roster), registered in `SETUP.md`'s harness table and conformant to the ADR-005 setup contract. Getting there **first requires laying a shared adapter-contract foundation** so the OpenCode adapter (and future ones) is a thin rendering layer, not a copy of the Mirai adapter. Done = OpenCode adapter buildable against a shared core, with the generic/harness-specific seam drawn and recorded in an ADR.

## Notes

- **Domain:** loom is a content-only SDLC agent framework. An *adapter* renders loom's generic primitives into a *harness*'s native config. See `AGENTS.md`, `SPEC.md`, `wiki/glossary/index.md` (Harness, Adapter, Setup contract).
- **This is the "one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real" moment** (`SKILLS/design/codebase-design`). Mirai is the only adapter today; OpenCode is the second, so the true seam becomes visible now — architecture-first per ADR-003.
- **Skills every session should consult:** `SKILLS/design/improve-codebase-architecture` (foundation work), `SKILLS/design/codebase-design` (deep-module vocabulary: depth, seam, deletion test), `SKILLS/discovery/grill-me` + `SKILLS/design/domain-model` (grilling tickets), `SKILLS/discovery/research` (research tickets), `SKILLS/design/design-an-interface` (shared-core interface).
- **Standing preference:** ORDER = foundation refactor BEFORE building OpenCode (user decision, ADR-003). OMO is an **opt-in layer** of the OpenCode adapter (like `docs-lookup` is opt-in in Mirai), not mandatory — a bare-OpenCode project must not be forced into OMO.
- **Key seam hypothesis:** generic core = stage groupings + skill rosters + capability-per-role + model archetypes + most interview tables + 5-step contract + init/update modes. Harness-specific = native primitive names, frontmatter/config formats, capability→tool table, verify checklist, templates, output locations. Model-archetype RENDER TARGET differs: Mirai=inline `model:` per agent; OpenCode/OMO=central `oh-my-openagent.json`.
- **Reference adapter to mirror:** `adapters/mirai/` = setup.md, MAPPING.md, STAGES.md, references/{interview,capabilities,write-format,verify}.md, assets/templates/*.
- **PR #1 disposition:** user will close it; OMO patterns already absorbed (this session). OMO = OpenCode CLI plugin by SST (opencode.ai); config `opencode.json` / `~/.config/opencode/`; `.claude` compat layer for migration.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index — one line per closed ticket -->

- [Research: OpenCode native primitives](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/5) — OpenCode ≈ Mirai/Claude: skills use identical agentskills.io format (name==folder); agents are `.opencode/agents/*.md` (or `opencode.json`) with `permission`-based tool control (`edit:deny` = the withhold); commands = `.opencode/commands/*.md`; `AGENTS.md` for always-on context; built-in `plan` agent = the read-only `Plan` analogue; built-in `explore`/`scout` subagents. GAPS: no harness memory tool (persist→committed folder), no description-triggered per-file instructions.
- [Research: OMO model-tiering config](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/6) — **config file is `omo.json`/`omo.jsonc` (NOT `oh-my-openagent.json`, which is legacy/migration-only)**, harness-spanning, in `.omo/` or `~/.omo/`. Has `models` catalog + `categories` (task tiers) + `agents` (overlay OMO builtins). OMO's "models are developers" = loom's 3 archetypes exactly (Sisyphus=Communicator, Hephaestus=Deep Specialist, Explore=Utility). Canonical field is `reasoning` (not deprecated `variant`). Recommend OMO layer OVERRIDES models on OMO builtins rather than redefining loom's roster.
- [Draw the generic-vs-harness-specific seam in adapters/mirai/](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/4) — the seam is **generic vocabulary/obligation + per-adapter render-binding port**, a shape that recurs 3× (model, capability, seam-artifact) → the seam is *real*, not hypothetical. Shared core renders **6 primitives** (skill, stage-agent [utilities fold in — not a 7th], stage-prompt, capability, instruction/protocol-doc, model-archetype); **3 render-binding ports** attach to capability/instruction/model-archetype (capability→tool, seam-obligation→wiring, archetype→model). Clean generic: stage groupings, skill rosters, capability-*sets*, interview *questions*, contract prose, init/update, provenance discipline, invariant-checks. Clean specific: native names, output locations, base-agent names, templates, format-checks. `verify.md` splits (generic invariants + specific format-checks). Holds for next ~5–10 adapters.
- [Design the shared adapter-contract interface](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/7) — **Design B** (prose contract enumerating named port-obligations; templates stay adapter-private) over "filled-in template pack", because SPEC forbids harness detail in shared docs. Core lives in a **new top-level `contract/`** dir (not under `adapters/`, not in `workflows/`); `SETUP.md` stays front door + gains a pointer in. Core PROVIDES the generic content (5-step contract, init/update, 6 primitives + rosters/capability-sets/interview questions/invariant-checks); an adapter MUST SUPPLY **4 named obligations** — `capability→tool`, `archetype→model`, `seam-obligation→wiring` + a `primitive→file` manifest — as **prose tables** (no schema). Consumption = **reference, never copy** (setup.md goes thin). Kept deliberately minimal: contract *states* obligations, doesn't prescribe adapter file layout, so the seam is cheap to redraw. SPEC "conformance" gains one bullet. Graduated → [#8](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/8) (ADR-013) + [#9](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/9) (build core + refactor Mirai).
- [Write ADR-013: the shared adapter-contract core](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/8) — recorded the #7 design as **ADR-013** (extends ADR-005): prose port-obligations (Design B) over a template pack; core in a new top-level `contract/`; PROVIDES the generic 5-step contract + 6 primitives, adapter MUST SUPPLY 4 named obligations; reference-never-restate; SPEC conformance bullet added. `validate.sh` passes. Design-only — migration is #9.
- [Build the shared adapter-contract core (contract/) + refactor Mirai to reference it](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/9) — **foundation built.** Created top-level `contract/` (index=5-step contract+init/update+safety; primitives=6 primitives+stage groupings+skill rosters+capability-sets+archetypes; interview=generic questions; discipline=provenance/idempotency+generic invariant-checks; PORTS=the 4 obligations as prose). Refactored `adapters/mirai/` to **reference, never restate** — `setup.md` 211→128 lines, `STAGES.md` 284→107, `interview.md` 153→55; `verify.md` split (generic invariants→core, Mirai format-checks local). Wired `SETUP.md` Step-2 pointer + SPEC conformance bullet + `index.md` registration + `validate.sh` link-check. `validate.sh` green (945 links). Graduated → [#10](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/10) (build OpenCode against the core).
- [Build the OpenCode adapter (adapters/opencode/) against contract/, with opt-in OMO layer](https://github.com/zentetsukenz/agent/issues/10) — **DESTINATION REACHED.** Built `adapters/opencode/` as loom's **second** adapter — a thin layer that references `contract/` and restates none of it. Four ports for OpenCode: `capability→tool` = `permission:` key, **withhold = `deny`** (inverse of Mirai's omit-the-alias), `interview` = the **native `question` tool**, `persist` GAP = committed `.loom/handoffs/` + scoped-edit glob; `archetype→model` = inline `model: provider/model-id` **or** opt-in `omo.json` (canonical `reasoning`; OMO overlays its builtins, never forced on a bare project); `seam→wiring` = committed ledger + `opencode.json` `instructions:` pointer + human `Tab`-selected DISCOVER transition (no `handoffs:` primitive, no memory tool); `primitive→file` = skills→`.opencode/skills/`, stage agents→`mode:primary`, utilities→`mode:subagent`, quick→`.opencode/commands/`, base agents `plan`/`build`. Added `wiki/environments/opencode.md`, ADR-014, SETUP row, SPEC conformance section, `validate_opencode_config`. `validate.sh` green (1235 links). The two sub-fog items resolved inline (omo.json shapes → `references/omo.md`; instruction/interview GAP → native `question` + committed `protocol.md`).

## Out of scope

- **Shipping loom as a TypeScript/npm OMO-style plugin with a runtime** (ADR-001 Path X/Z). Rejected as destination: breaks loom's content-only identity. This effort renders *native config an agent writes*, not a runtime plugin.
- **A VS Code chat-extension** (`@engineer` participant + LM tools, from PR #1's VS-CODE-AI-EXTENSION.md). Out of scope: it's a distribution experiment orthogonal to an OpenCode adapter, and Mirai already IS loom's VS Code harness.
